text:
Maria: Heads-up — I'm iterating on the new experiment-creator flow in Console. Need input on routing defaults and guard behavior.
AJ: What's the primary risk we want to defend against by default? accidental large traffic to untested variants or capacity blowouts?
Sasha: Both. Also want clear telemetry tags so SRE/product can slice perf by variant/model/route.
Maria: UX objective: safe-by-default. Proposed rules: require a minimum sample per variant (e.g., 1k requests or 10k tokens) before allowing >20% traffic, and block >20% immediate jumps without a warmup canary.
Tom: Warmup schedule suggestion: auto-prefill ramp [1%,5%,15%,30%] with 10m per step. Console should allow override but show strong warnings.
AJ: For API shape, surface explicit weights plus optional ramp_schedule. Example: 
```json
{
  "variants": [
    {"id":"base","weight":9000},
    {"id":"quant-4bit","weight":1000}
  ],
  "ramp_schedule": [{"duration_minutes":10, "target_weight":1000}]
}
```
Weights are integers out of 10000 to avoid floating precision.
Maria: Two policy questions: 1) enforce guards in Console only or also at API layer for non-console clients? 2) Present guard failures as blocking or permissive warnings?
Sasha: Telemetry: emit experiment.created, experiment.ramp.step, experiment.traffic_change_blocked with tags: team, route, model_family, variant_id, reason, region. Also emit quality.sample_size metric for each variant so alerts can be gated.
Elaine: deploy-bot will run a precheck on each ramp step to validate capacity + SLA headroom. If blocked, return 409 with structured error.
AJ: Error contract: 409 + body { "code": "RAMP_BLOCKED", "reason": "insufficient_capacity", "details": "pool eu-west-1 at 92% GPU" }. Console should render actionable copy.
Maria: Suggested Console copy: \"Change blocked: pool capacity insufficient — reduce target weight or add burst capacity (learn more)\" with a link to capacity recommendations.
Tom: Another guard: minimum sustained throughput per variant — disallow ramps that would result in <50 rps for 10m to avoid noisy metrics.
Sasha: Also flag low sample size for quality checks so alerts won't fire until sample thresholds met. Add a `quality_sample` tag to telemetry events.
AJ: Implementation note for router: we use integer split boundaries [0..10000) and fast integer hashing. Document that Console weights map directly to split ranges — no hidden normalization.
Maria: UX idea: show estimated RPS per variant (based on historical route traffic) and color rows red/orange/green depending on whether thresholds are met.
Elaine: deploy-bot:precheck result returned OK for initial schedule but warns: capacity margin low in region=eu-west-1. Recommendation: add +2000 burst capacity or reduce peak target.
AJ: Should Console silently add a ramp_schedule when a user omits it? I vote prefill sensible steps but require explicit approval to delete.
Maria: Agreed. Prefill [1,5,15,30], show compressed summary: \"0 -> 30% over 40m (4 steps)\" with quick-edit.
Tom: Audit logs: every weight/state transition must be recorded with actor, timestamp, before/after, and action reason. Product needs this for audits.
Sasha: Add boolean `auto_approved` when an admin bypasses guards; telemetry/audit should record who auto-approved.
AJ: I'll draft a short RFC with JSON examples, error codes, and router mapping. Will post link here.
Maria: Thanks — I'll wire the UI mock to AJ's draft and add a telemetry checklist. PR incoming. :party_parrot:
Elaine: I'll add capacity checks to the precheck job and link to the docs. Follow-ups: unit tests for integer-weight hashing and a telemetry QA run.
deploy-bot: precheck: capacity_warning(eu-west-1): true, recommended_action: \"add_burst_2k_or_reduce_peak\"
Maria: Great, keep the notes here and tag me when the RFC is up.
